top_news.summary: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Whitney Tilson, Stansberry Research Editor, and Stephanie Guild, Robinhood CIO. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
top_news.summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. top_news.title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
top_news.summary: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: 'Notes on Being a Man', 'The Invisible Hand'
top_news.summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss 'Notes on Being a Man' by Scott Galloway and 'The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth: How a Nineteenth-Century Novelist Taught the World Economics' by Jeanna Smialek. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: US Family Annual Healthcare Plan Now Costs More Than $28K
top_news.summary: Bloomberg's John Tozzi joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The annual cost of a US family’s employer-provided healthcare plan reached an average $28,303 this year, 5% more than 2025, according to an annual survey conducted by health policy nonprofit KFF. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: The Circuit - Season 6 Trailer
top_news.summary: A Bloomberg Originals series hosted by Emily Chang that goes behind the scenes with founders, influencers and innovators. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Robin Wigglesworth on the Importance of Curiosity
top_news.summary:
Barry speaks with Robin Wigglesworth, editor of Financial Times' Alphaville blog and author of the new book 'A Fabulous Debt: The Epic Story of How Bonds Built the Modern World'. They discuss the bond market as the engine of the global economy, why the 30-year mortgage is "a miracle of the modern world," and when we should actually start worrying about US debt.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: National Wealth Tax Could Work: Tilson
top_news.summary: Whitney Tilson, editor for Stansberry Research, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Tilson's hopes to bring Democrats back to the center, his personal investing strategy, and the potential for a national wealth tax.  (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: San Diego to Leave Muni Bond Group After SEC Oversight Concerns
top_news.summary: The city of San Diego said it plans to withdraw from a group that helps issue and manage billions of dollars in municipal bonds after federal regulators raised concerns about the organization’s oversight.

top_news.title: Chipmakers Post Longest Weekly Drop Since November
top_news.summary: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the Federal Reserve decision on interest rates. Brent crude settled near $117 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened supplies. Most S&P 500 firms fell even as selling pressure on tech shares abated.
